card.name: Eskista
card.era: ancient (traced by some to the Axumite era)
card.profile: Eskista (Amharic for 'dancing shoulders') is a traditional dance of the Amhara of Ethiopia, also strongly associated with Tigray. Per Wikipedia, it is built on rapid, rhythmic rolling and bouncing of the shoulders plus chest and neck movements, performed to traditional instruments such as the masinqo (one-string fiddle), krar (lyre) and kebero (drum). A staple of weddings and festivals, it often features shilimat, where admirers stick money to the best dancer's forehead. Folklore links its snake-like neck motion to mimicking a serpent.
card.insight: Considered one of the most technically demanding African dances, eskista is Ethiopia's most iconic dance and has gone global (Wikipedia; Lakewood Center for the Arts).
